PullRequest.Title: Update Foundry Local SDK to 2.1.0
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- update `foundry-local-sdk` and the packaged dictation runtime from 2.0.1 to 2.1.0
- pick up upstream live-audio language forwarding fixes from microsoft/Foundry-Local#1064 and microsoft/Foundry-Local#1138
- align dictation runtime packaging tests with ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 and ONNX Runtime GenAI 0.17.1

SDK 2.0.1 exposed `session.settings.language` but dropped it in the live transcription adapter, while its native streaming path did not bind the request language to Nemotron's `lang_id`. SDK 2.1.0 fixes both layers and normalizes canonical language tags such as `es-US` before lookup.

## Testing

- `node --test build/lib/test/dictationRuntime.test.ts`
- `npm run eslint -- build/lib/test/dictationRuntime.test.ts`
- `cd build && npm run typecheck`
- verified the installed 2.1.0 runtime layout and VS Code native-loader patch

Fixes #341152

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The cache-key flow and absence of version eviction are explicit in repository code, and first-use reachability is confirmed through the local dictation start path. Exact compressed/uncompressed artifact sizes are not recorded in source, which affects magnitude but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: versioned native-runtime bytes on disk and one replacement CDN transfer
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each foundry-local-sdk version used for on-device dictation creates another `<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/<version>` tree; because only staging and partial-download paths are removed, retained bytes grow linearly with SDK upgrades used on that profile.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Persistent duplicate native-runtime storage and repeated full runtime download/write cost after upgrades, eventually increasing disk pressure and risking cache writes failing on constrained profiles.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With the 2.0.1 pin, an already provisioned `<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/2.0.1` was a verified cache hit and no new runtime directory or CDN transfer was needed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new 2.1.0 pin is read by `getRuntimeVersion()`, stamped into `product.dictationRuntime`, and passed to `ensureFoundryLocalRuntime`, which now provisions `<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/2.1.0`; the existing 2.0.1 directory is left untouched.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Changing `foundry-local-sdk` from 2.0.1 to 2.1.0 at package.json:148 directly changes the versioned cache directory and makes the prior 2.0.1 payload unreachable from the updated product while leaving it retained.
Findings.Title: Evict superseded dictation runtime versions
Findings.Impact: A user who has used on-device dictation before upgrading pays a full native-runtime download/extraction on first use and permanently retains both the old and new ONNX/Foundry payloads. The same accumulation repeats on later SDK updates.
Findings.Evidence: `build/dictation-runtime/common.ts:getRuntimeVersion` reads this exact dependency pin; `produce.ts` stamps it into the product; `LocalTranscriptionService` passes that version to `ensureFoundryLocalRuntime`; and `foundryLocalRuntime.ts` derives `overrideDir = join(cacheRoot, download.version)`. Repository-wide searches show removals only for staging/temp/partial target paths, with no cleanup of sibling version directories. The payload contains two N-API addons plus Foundry Local, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime GenAI shared libraries, so this is substantial retained data rather than metadata.
Findings.Recommendation: When provisioning 2.1.0 succeeds, prune superseded sibling version directories under `chatDictationRuntime` with cross-process-safe, age-based retention (for example, keep the current and recently used version for rollback), rather than deleting only staging data.

Scenarios.Scenario: First on-device dictation after updating from a build that provisioned Foundry Local 2.0.1
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer starts capture immediately, but first transcript/session readiness waits for utility-process IPC, `ensureFoundryLocalRuntime`, SDK import and manager creation, model catalog lookup/download if needed, and native model/session load. The changed runtime version makes provisioning a cache miss, so the CDN download, filesystem write, extraction, verification, and publish are on the critical path to transcription even though audio is buffered meanwhile.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start and stream local transcription through a lazily created utility process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker/channel per window on first local-transcription use, then one start call per dictation session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical lazy utility-process boundary with SDK 2.0.1
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Worker creation and start dispatch precede local model/session readiness, though capture begins while preparation continues

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the platform-specific versioned native runtime tarball from the VS Code CDN
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful transfer per process racing on a cold profile/version/platform; zero on a warm 2.1.0 cache hit
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An existing 2.0.1 cache was a hit and performed no runtime transfer; changing the key to 2.1.0 forces a replacement transfer
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks SDK manager/session creation and therefore first transcript availability

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write tarball, extract native libraries to staging, verify files, atomically publish, and write completion marker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full payload write/extraction per cold download, plus bounded existence checks for six or seven required files on every ensure
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A warm 2.0.1 profile only performed marker/file checks; 2.1.0 creates and writes a separate tree
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold extraction is on the path to manager creation; warm existence checks remain small and bounded

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the Foundry model catalog and download the selected model on a model-cache miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalog lookup per service model load and at most one model download, coalesced by `_modelPromise`
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same model lookup/download behavior under SDK 2.0.1; the diff provides no evidence of changed request count
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks native model/session readiness after runtime provisioning

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain extracted Foundry Local, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime GenAI libraries under each SDK-version directory
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete platform payload retained for every SDK version first used by the profile
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the existing 2.0.1 payload was needed; this update adds 2.1.0 without evicting 2.0.1
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Retention is off the immediate critical path after provisioning but accumulates persistent disk pressure

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One native runtime payload for the current platform per SDK version and user profile; model work is one selected model. Concurrent windows can each initiate the same first-use payload download because coalescing is process-local.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Audio appends are serialized. Runtime provisioning coalesces to one promise per library path inside one utility process, but separate VS Code windows have separate utility processes and may download concurrently; a filesystem publish lock prevents conflicting final replacement, not duplicate transfers. NuGet/build concurrency is not involved at runtime.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the diff, a previously provisioned 2.0.1 directory was a warm verified hit. The 2.1.0 pin changes both CDN and cache keys, producing a cold miss while retaining the 2.0.1 sibling indefinitely. Later 2.1.0 sessions verify the marker/files and are warm hits. In-process requests coalesce; cross-process requests download separately and only serialize final publication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed manifest pin is explicitly the source of the stamped runtime version, the runtime joins that version into the cache path, and no sibling-version eviction exists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository does not record the compressed or extracted payload size, and not every user enables on-device dictation. The payload composition proves it is substantial native data, but exact disk and first-use latency vary by platform/network.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: this upgrade necessarily creates a new runtime cache entry for prior users but never retires the now-unreachable old entry, so retained native payload bytes grow with upgrades.

Scenarios.Scenario: Subsequent on-device dictation sessions on Foundry Local 2.1.0
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Utility-process start, bounded cache verification, lazy SDK/manager initialization, model catalog/load, and session start remain on the path to transcript readiness; the native-runtime CDN transfer and extraction are off the path after the first successful provision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check the completion marker and required native library files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed seven-or-fewer existence checks per model ensure, with no collection-dependent fan-out
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fixed checks occurred against the 2.0.1 directory
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small bounded work before SDK manager creation

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send start/audio/stop calls and transcription events across the utility-process channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One start and stop per session and one IPC call per audio chunk/result event
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Audio and result delivery use this existing boundary throughout the session

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Catalog query and optional model download
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one lookup/load per selected model per utility-process lifetime; download only on a model-cache miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same call shape and coalescing with 2.0.1
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model load remains on session-readiness path; warm model data avoids the large download

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active singleton dictation session per renderer; audio chunks scale with recording duration and are serialized through one append chain. Runtime verification scales with a fixed required-file list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active session, serialized appends, one model preparation promise, and one in-process runtime provisioning promise. Separate windows remain independent utility processes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The 2.1.0 completion marker plus required files form a positive cache hit. The in-memory model promise coalesces same-model loads for the utility-process lifetime, and model files persist in their separate cache. No negative runtime cache is present, so failed provisioning retries on later starts as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the unchanged call path and bounded cache checks; insufficient evidence for any additional SDK-internal regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native execution cost may differ internally between opaque SDK versions, but the supplied diff and lockfile do not expose evidence of increased per-chunk CPU, allocations, or boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: after the new cache is warm, cardinality, coalescing, IPC, and visible scheduling remain unchanged in the supplied code.

Scenarios.Scenario: Publish-build production of the per-platform dictation runtime
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each supported build target, the publish job copies SDK native files, sequentially downloads two pinned NuGet packages, extracts matching libraries, gzip-compresses the payload, hashes it, performs upload existence checking, and uploads when absent. Packaging then stamps the resulting 2.1.0 URL template.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the authenticated NuGet service index and download ONNX Runtime plus ONNX Runtime GenAI packages
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One service-index request and two sequential package downloads per target build, subject to existing bounded retries
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two calls occurred for versions 1.28.0 and 0.15.2; only artifact versions change to 1.30.0 and 0.17.1
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All downloads and extraction must complete before tarball creation

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy native SDK files, extract NuGet libraries, gzip the tree, hash and stat the tarball
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One staging tree and one tarball per target job
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same operations and cardinality for the 2.0.1 payload

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check and upload the versioned runtime tarball to CDN storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HEAD decision and at most one upload per target/version
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: 2.0.1 already addressed existing CDN objects; 2.1.0 requires a new object, as expected for changed native binaries
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publish completion waits for the versioned artifact to exist

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one target per platform build job, two NuGet artifacts per target, and one tarball/CDN object per supported target and SDK version; five target jobs may operate independently in the pipeline.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two NuGet artifacts are fetched sequentially inside each target build. Different platform jobs may run concurrently; there is no newly introduced per-item Promise fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The NuGet service index is cached only within one `fetchDependencyLibraries` invocation. CDN upload uses HEAD-based idempotence for reruns. The version change intentionally selects a new CDN object and does not reuse 2.0.1 bytes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: source establishes exact boundary counts and sequential scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The newer NuGet/package byte sizes are not present in the diff, so no claim about increased build duration or artifact size is supportable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate reportable build regression: boundary cardinality and concurrency are unchanged, and producing one new versioned payload is required by the dependency update.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repository dependency installation and postinstall patching
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Package installation fetches the new SDK tarball and runs its allowed install script; VS Code postinstall then reads and patches the SDK native loader in root and remote node_modules when present.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the pinned foundry-local-sdk 2.1.0 package during dependency installation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One package fetch on npm cache miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single package fetch targeted 2.0.1

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read, transform, and write up to two SDK native loader files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most root and remote copies; zero writes when already marked

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pinned package tarball and at most two loader files per repository install.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Controlled by the existing package manager; VS Code's two patch targets are processed sequentially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: npm's package cache may serve the 2.1.0 tarball after first fetch; the VS Code patch is marker-idempotent. The lockfile retains the same dependency set and install-script shape as 2.0.1.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for repository-owned patching and lockfile dependency shape; low for opaque SDK-internal install work, which is therefore not reported.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external package's install-script internals and tarball byte delta are not exposed in the supplied repository diff, so an install-time regression cannot be established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable install-time performance regression is proven beyond the expected one-time fetch of a newly pinned package.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced runtime, build/publish, install, IPC, network, filesystem, cache, and concurrency paths. Submitted one medium-confidence-impact/high-mechanism-confidence cache-lifecycle finding for retained superseded native runtime versions; found no evidenced SDK-internal, warm-session, build-fanout, or install-time regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
